title: sre-weekly-reliability-deep-dive-prep-2026-07-10
content:
Context / goal:
- Prep notes for SRE weekly reliability deep-dive (short, action-oriented). Focus: recent paging trends, SLO burn drivers, and two top incidents for postmortem follow-up.
- Outcome for this meeting: (1) agree owner/due dates for mitigation tasks, (2) pick 2 small experiments to reduce p99 latency tail, (3) confirm runbook updates for KV cache + autoscaler interactions.

High-level summary (quick bullets to open with):
- Pager volume: down ~12% week-over-week, but high-severity spikes concentrated in two patterns: long-running KV-cache evictions and autoscaler race conditions during bursts.
- SLOs: infra-api error budget at 76% remaining (monthly window), hosted-generation p99 latency has used ~36% of error budget this week (not yet critical, but trend is upward).
- Two incidents to prioritize: INC-2026-07-03-KVLEAK (KV cache growth causing OOMs on worker pool) and INC-2026-07-07-AUTO-RACE (autoscaler mis-scaling causing cold starts + timeouts).

Metrics to bring / slides to show (exact numbers below to copy into slide):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for hosted-generation (7d rolling): p50=82ms, p95=210ms, p99=920ms (spike window shows 1.6s peaks).
- Token throughput: 1.2M tokens/min sustained; burst peaks 2.4M tokens/min (these correlate with autoscaler issues).
- Paging: total pages 42 (last 7d) vs 48 (previous 7d). Sev1/2 pages: 6 (down from 9).
- Errors: 5xx rate for runtime endpoints 0.27% (baseline target <=0.2%).

Incident summaries (short):
1) INC-2026-07-03-KVLEAK (owner: Jordan K.)
   - What happened: one worker pool (us-west-2-gpu-b) started accumulating KV-cache entries and did not evict as expected; memory grew over hours and several pods OOMKilled, triggering cascading falls back to fallback-model that has higher latency.
   - Impact: increased p99 latency for requests routed to that pool; 3 customer-facing errors; multiple pages during 02:10-04:45 UTC.
   - Hypothesis: regression in KV eviction heuristics introduced in runtime PR#1287 (recent change to LRU sampling). Also autoscaler interaction: heavy eviction meant GC CPU spikes which delayed heartbeats.
   - Immediate mitigation taken: drained that pool, disabled the new eviction flag, scaled up a fresh pool with conservative eviction config.
   - Next actions (from initial post-incident triage): add unit test for eviction edge case, add a metric for KV growth rate, and add alert when worker mem growth > 70% for >10m.

2) INC-2026-07-07-AUTO-RACE (owner: Luis O.)
   - What happened: rapid incoming burst caused autoscaler to start scale-up, but scale decisions raced with the new warmup policy; several requests hit cold workers leading to timeouts and retries which amplified load.
   - Impact: request timeouts (some customers retried at client layer causing duplicate downstream load), p95 increased from 210ms to 480ms during 11:30-12:15 UTC.
   - Hypothesis: warmup threshold too aggressive + longer container startup times after recent base-image change.
   - Mitigation: temporarily bumped min replicas for heavy-traffic queues; reverted base-image layering change.
   - Next actions: measure true cold-start duration (instrument start-to-ready), add autoscaler safety buffer for bursty queues, and create a synthetic spike test to validate warmup.

Open questions to cover in meeting:
- For KV leak: do we keep the evict-flag off by default until we ship a guarded rollout? pros/cons. (My leaning: gated rollout with observability first).
- For autoscaler: what is acceptable extra capacity buffer for bursty customers (2x? 1.5x?), and can we make it dynamic per queue?
- Should we add a short-term SLO tweak to avoid customer-impacting 4xx/5xx during rollout windows (e.g., planned maintenance window exclusion)?

Proposed agenda (20–30m):
1) Quick metrics drop (5m) — p99 trend, paging heatmap, SLO burn summary.
2) Incident 1 deep-dive (8–10m) — Jordan to present hypothesis + rollout plan for fix.
3) Incident 2 deep-dive (8–10m) — Luis to present autoscaler experiment & playbook updates.
4) Action-item agreement and owners (5m).

Action items (capture + owners) — propose these during meeting and lock down:
- A1: Add KV growth rate and eviction-failure alert to observability (Prom alert + dashboard). Owner: Jordan K. Due: 2026-07-14.
- A2: Revert evict-flag merge to feature-branch; create canary plan (5% traffic) with telemetry. Owner: Ayesha M. Due: 2026-07-13.
- A3: Instrument container cold-start from process start -> ready, add metric to startup histogram. Owner: Luis O. Due: 2026-07-17.
- A4: Create synthetic spike test harness that can run in staging and reproduce autoscale behavior. Owner: Eng-tools (suggested: Priya R.). Due: 2026-07-21.
- A5: Update runbook pages: KV cache section, autoscaler playbook (clear steps for draining/rollback). Owner: Documentation SRE (assign: Mei Chen). Due: 2026-07-16.

Notes / things to capture in post-meeting follow-up (my personal TODOs):
- Collect traces for a representative request during the 07-03 KV incident (trace ids: try to pull 03:40 UTC traces).
- Pull memory/GC profiles for drained pool; compare to healthy pool on 07-01 baseline.
- Draft short email to customer-success for impacted customers (Jordan to draft).

Risk/concerns to call out quickly:
- Rolling back eviction heuristics could expose higher token cost (more cache misses) for a short window; balance cost vs stability.
- Autoscaler buffer increases cost (extra reserved capacity). Need to quantify cost delta before committing.

Hand-off checklist (for each owner above):
- Confirm PRs needed (link in follow-up) and required reviewers.
- Add acceptance criteria for canary (telemetry thresholds, rollback triggers).
- Put calendar hold for a coordinated rollout if we do a widened canary (ops on-call + SRE).

Quick reference (things to paste into the meeting doc):
- SLOs: hosted-generation availability target 99.9% (monthly), infra-api target 99.5% (monthly).
- Current infra-api availability this month: 99.45% (2 incidents counting).
- Suggested rollback triggers for canary: 5xx rate >0.5% OR p99 latency increase >2x baseline for >10m.

Misc scratch ideas (not for meeting unless time):
- Explore a tiny in-proc KV eviction watchdog that can self-heal before OOM.
- Add token-budget-aware autoscaler policy (scale more aggressively for high-throughput token workloads vs many short requests).

Endnotes / links to paste into the formal notes after meeting:
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287
- Incident ticket IDs: SRE-4312 (KV leak), SRE-4330 (autoscaler race)
- Confluence: /pages/SRE-weekly-ops-2026-07-10

Personal follow-up (me):
- Run a quick heater test in staging today (10–15m) to validate that braking the evict-flag reduces mem growth. If green, propose 5% canary tomorrow.
- Ping Priya on spike harness status and see if a minimal harness can be borrowed from chaos infra.

-- Ayesha
(Notes: this is a scratchpad — will convert to meeting doc + action tracker after the sync)
